claim: *Active and passive alignment.* Active alignment uses a model and its alignment mechanisms to transform a realization until the modeled obligations are satisfied. Once correspondence has been established, those models and mechanisms remain in the governed engineering environment as passive alignment: subsequent changes are evaluated against the established obligations so that correspondence is preserved.
topology: Two sequential panels; active compare/modify/evaluate feedback then passive change/evaluate feedback with retained models.
required_terms: Once active alignment succeeds, retain the models and mechanisms.
Models, mechanisms, and governance remain as engineering capital for every change.
bw_encoding: Black strokes and text; pale gray headers only. Dashed paths retain optional, missing, or forbidden semantics where explicitly labeled. Position, containment, line weight, and written labels carry distinctions without color.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames.
alt:
Two stacked panels. Top, active alignment (convergence): models M feed a pipeline of
    compare (detect gaps), modify (with agents), and evaluate (check alignment), producing the aligned
    system S-prime; a loop-back arrow labelled repeat until correspondence returns from evaluate to
    compare. A handoff arrow labelled once active alignment succeeds leads to the bottom panel, passive
    alignment (preservation): a proposed change delta-S enters evaluate (check against models), with the
    retained models M feeding in from above; the outcome is admit or reject, yielding the updated system
    S-prime, with a loop labelled continue protecting correspondence returning to the next proposed
    change. A closing note: the models, mechanisms, and governance remain in the governed engineering
    environment as engineering capital.
